> 
> P1-1 (confirms orchestrator note a). Plan point 5; model/src/kernel.rs:997-1004. The plan's 'separate overlap helper' never touches alloc_va. alloc_va still takes `above` from p.space.last_key_value(), and map_fixed's pages go into p.space, so the divergence stays. Attack: map_fixed(USER_TOP-0x1000, 0x1000, R), then map_anon(0x1000, RW). Model: start = vpn(USER_TOP), start+1 > vpn(USER_TOP), so OutOfMemory. Kernel: map_run -> find_virtual_address scans [mem_default_base, +256 MiB) (kernel/src/mem.rs:388-392) and succeeds. Every alloc_va user (received buffers etc.) diverges the same way, and a static ELF linked high is exactly what the stub places. Fix: alloc_va keeps above-highest when that fits; otherwise it takes the first gap of n free vpns in [KERNEL_CHOSEN_BASE, USER_TOP) from p.space.range(..), and returns OutOfMemory only if no gap exists. Existing traces don't change: when the fallback fails it gives the same OutOfMemory that the charge after it would have given. Add a model test for this trace.
> 
> P1-2 (note b). Plan steps 2 and 4; kernel/src/arch/riscv/mem.rs:125-143 and 639. The plan calls address_available_in once per page over the whole range, then runs tables_needed over the whole range, both before any budget bound. Attack on rv64: map_fixed(0x1000, 0x40_0000_0000-0x1000, R) from an empty process with any budget costs about 2^26 walks plus 2^27 tables_needed iterations in the kernel before it returns OutOfMemory, and it can be repeated. Every existing range loop is bounded: unmap and process_map stop at the first page the caller doesn't own, which the caller's budget bounds, and find_virtual_address is limited to a 256 MiB window. REFUTE the 'cheap npages > free_pages check first' variant: it changes the observable result. A range that both overlaps a mapping and exceeds the budget must return InvalidArgument (Errors row: range before OutOfMemory), and that variant would return OutOfMemory. Fix, same error order and bounded: (i) an occupancy walk that skips absent subtrees. When the level-L table is missing, jump to the next level-L boundary (Sv39: 1 GiB or 2 MiB; Sv32: 4 MiB). The cost is at most the root entries plus 512 x the tables present in the range, and those tables are charged to the caller. This is a new arch helper, e.g. range_available_in, so the plan's 'no new function' changes. (ii) Split the charge check the way the row reads: npages > free is OutOfMemory (pages), then npages + tables_needed > free is OutOfMemory (page tables). tables_needed then walks at most free_pages pages. Model: use p.space.range(first..first+n).next().is_none() rather than a loop over each vpn.
> 
> P2-3. Plan check order step 3, and 'check_permissions runs a second time inside map_page_inner'. KERNEL-SPEC.md:435-436 says the mapping code refuses W+X again so the rule doesn't rest on the decode check alone. Under this plan that second refusal happens inside map_page_inner, after the charge and under .expect, so it would panic the kernel after charging instead of refusing. Fix: map_fixed's own flag check includes W+X, copying process_map's three-way check (kernel/src/process.rs:354-358), and it runs before anything is charged. The model calls decode_flags first, as map_anon and set_flags do.
> 
> P2-4 (note c). Confirmed, with one caveat. After the charge check nothing can fail. User space has no superpage leaves on either width, since the physmap is in the kernel half (libs/abi/src/arch/riscv/mem.rs:15-50), so walk can only fail on OutOfMemory. tables_needed counts each missing table exactly once, including across root entries, on Sv39 (3 levels) and Sv32 (2 levels): a contiguous range always moves the index from 511 to 0 at a boundary, so comparing against the last counted index cannot miss a table. map_page_in's is_occupied cannot fire on a page that the stricter address_available_in found empty. check_permissions cannot fire once P2-3 is in. Caveat: alloc_page -> alloc_frame can still fail when physical RAM runs out. The .expect is sound only if every budget's free_pages is backed by free frames. process_map's .expect at process.rs:382-392 relies on the same unstated assumption, so name it in the expect text. Also use one address space throughout: map_page_inner writes to current_root(), so pass MemoryMapping::current() to address_available_in, tables_needed and prepare_map, or map with map_into_with(space) as process_map does.
> 
> P2-5 (note d). Gaps in the map-fixed-attack.rs list:
>  a. Partial overlap: [free, free, occupied] and [occupied, free], with budget_usage unchanged after each.
>  b. An untouched legacy reservation (an IncreaseHeap page never faulted in). This is the one case where address_available_in and is_occupied disagree, and it must be refused.
>  c. The exact budget boundary on a range that crosses a 2 MiB leaf-table boundary where tables are missing: free == npages+tables succeeds, and free == npages+tables-1 fails with usage unchanged.
>  d. The success path: pages read as zero, flags are enforced (a write to an R page faults), and unmap brings usage back to baseline, page tables included.
>  e. USER_AREA_END-0x1000 with len 0x1000 is accepted; addr == USER_AREA_END is refused.
>  f. The huge len from P1-2 returns promptly.
>  g. Unknown flag bits (8) return InvalidArgument.
>  h. map_anon still succeeds after a map_fixed inside the DEFAULT_BASE window, and after one near USER_AREA_END (the kernel half of P1-1).
>  i. The rv32 wrap case cannot run at boot, because acceptance is an rv64 boot plus an rv32 compile. Cover it with a host unit test of user_range at 32-bit widths, and don't list it as a boot case.
>  j. Name the Mutation variant (for example 'map_fixed skips the overlap check') and the trace that catches it.
>  The stub page, startup page and stack cases can only be checked on the kernel: the model has no stack or startup page in p.space, so don't claim model parity for them.
> 
> P3-6. Kernel residual, not K5a's to fix: the kernel's map_anon window is 256 MiB, so a map_fixed that fills it makes kernel map_anon fail with OutOfMemory where the model succeeds. That is the same divergence that already exists once map_anon totals exceed 256 MiB; record it as a residual.
> 
> Checked and fine: MapFixed = 26 follows SystemReset = 25 (libs/sys/src/call.rs:324, model/src/syscall.rs:200). Lent-in and lent-out pages have non-empty PTEs, and the model keeps them in p.space as LentIn/LentOut, so both kernel and model refuse them. A legacy IncreaseHeap into a map_fixed page is refused by reserve_address and rolled back (mem.rs:448-473; arch mem.rs:394). Overflow on rv32 and rv64 is caught by checked_add in user_range. addr 0 is left to K5a-addr0.

> Files/functions (updates from v1, same base list otherwise):
> 
> KERNEL
> - kernel/src/arch/riscv/mem.rs: NEW `range_available_in(space: &MemoryMapping, addr: usize, len: usize) -> bool`. Walks the page-table tree once, top-down: at each level, if `table.child(index)` is `None` (no subtree), the whole `leaf_size(level)`-sized gap from the current boundary counts as free (matches `walk(..., None)`'s Err=>available semantics used today) and the walk jumps straight to the next boundary at that level, without visiting any page under it; if a child exists it recurses one level down; at level 0 a nonempty PTE (`!pte.is_empty()`, so a `Pte::reservation` counts, same rule as `address_available_in`) makes the whole call return false immediately. Cost: at most the root entries spanned plus 512x the tables actually present in the range (P1-2(i)). Replaces the plan's per-page `address_available_in` loop for map_fixed only; `address_available_in` itself is untouched (process_map keeps using it).
> - kernel/src/mem.rs `MemoryManager::map_fixed`: new check order (all before any charge/mapping):
>   1. `Self::user_range(addr, len)` (align, len!=0, in user space incl. addr 0 per K5a-addr0 — no change needed, `user_range` already accepts 0).
>   2. `range_available_in(&space, addr, len)`, refuse `InvalidArgument` if false.
>   3. Flags: three-way check copying `process.rs:354-360` exactly (empty, W+X, W-without-R) -> `InvalidArgument`, run here so the later `.expect` can never see bad flags (P2-3; decode already blocks W+X/unknown bits, this is defense in depth like process_map's, not reliance on decode alone).
>   4. Cheap charge check: `npages as u64 > mm.free_pages(budget)` -> `OutOfMemory` ("pages"), *before* computing tables_needed, so a huge len that already fails on pages never reaches the O(pages) `tables_needed` walk (P1-2(ii)).
>   5. `tables_needed(&space, addr, npages)`; `npages as u64 + tables > free_pages(budget)` -> `OutOfMemory` ("page tables"). Bounded now because step 4 already capped npages at the budget.
>   6. Guaranteed-success loop: `prepare_map` then `alloc_page`+zero+`map_page_inner` per page, each `.expect("map_fixed: range_available_in, the flag check and the charge check above guarantee this; a budget's free_pages must be backed by free physical frames, the same assumption process_map's expect at process.rs:382-392 relies on")` (P2-4). One `let space = MemoryMapping::current();` used for every step 2/5/6 call (P2-4 consistency).
> - kernel/src/redoubt.rs: `Call::MapFixed{..}` arm, as v1.
> 
> REDOUBT-SYS: unchanged from v1 (MapFixed=26 in call.rs after SystemReset=25; error.rs InvalidArgument+OutOfMemory; ret.rs no-result group; tests.rs sample_calls()).

Add a trace test: map_fixed near USER_TOP then map_anon succeeds in both kernel and model.

### Red team · Reply

Event: `1ebaac42744eebc176068759269bb0de` · 2026-09-24T08:27:19Z

> K5a plan v2, red-team re-review. Merge verdict: OK with notes. P1-1, P1-2 and P2-3 to P2-5 are closed as I specified, and addr-0 is applied. Nothing new is wrong; the three notes below are P3.
> 
> Confirmed:
> (i) range_available_in skips absent subtrees correctly on Sv39 and Sv32. User space has no superpage leaves, so a missing child really does mean an empty range. The work is bounded by the root entries spanned plus the tables present in the range, which the caller pays for.
> (ii) The error order is kept: user_range, overlap, flags, then pages (OutOfMemory), then pages+tables (OutOfMemory). Both budget steps return the same code, so their split can't be seen from outside. The pages check caps tables_needed's work at the caller's free_pages, so a huge len now returns after a cheap root skip.
> (iii) The model and kernel give the same result at every step. decode_flags matches the kernel's decode (unknown bits, W+X). check_flags matches the kernel's three-way check; its W+X arm can't be reached after decode. The model's single n+tables charge and the kernel's two steps both return OutOfMemory. The overlap check agrees, because the model keeps LentIn and LentOut pages in p.space. Legacy reservations, stub, startup and stack pages are kernel-only, as the plan says.
> (iv) The W+X check runs before the charge, and the expect text names the assumption that budgets are backed by RAM.
> 
> N1 (P3), 'existing traces unchanged': true for the stored trace (model/traces) and the structured generator, whose process_map dst is 0x1000_0000+ (gen.rs:794), below KERNEL_CHOSEN_BASE. The raw generator's process_map dst can already put a child mapping near USER_TOP. There the fallback turns a model OutOfMemory into success, which is the kernel's answer. So a seeded test could change result, and if one does, the new result is correct. The same fix also closes this divergence, which predates map_fixed.
> N2 (P3), model map_fixed: return OutOfMemory when n > free before calling tables_needed. Without that, the hostile trace map_fixed(0, USER_TOP) puts 2^26 vpns through tables_needed's BTreeSet, and hostile replays must finish (hostile_traces_are_refused_cleanly). map_fresh already has the same cost, so fixing it there is optional.
> N3 (P3), range_available_in: fail closed when an entry above the leaf level is non-empty but not a table (child None and !is_empty) instead of skipping it. That can't happen today. If a user superpage ever existed, though, skipping would call the range free, and prepare_map's walk would then hit BadAddress under .expect. Also compute the jump as min((a | (span-1)) + 1, end), which can't wrap on either width because end <= USER_AREA_END. Sv32 tables have 1024 entries, not 512; that only affects the wording of the cost claim.
